minutes.headline: Stormwater task force found the consultant's draft fee tiers unclear and will seek clarification before the next meeting.
minutes.summary: The task force went through the consultant's first-draft stormwater utility rate structure. Members could not tell where multifamily, apartment, condo and commercial properties fall in the tiers, and thought too few large properties were counted. They worked backwards from a revenue target using the fee alternatives and Chapter 90, and discussed offsetting existing town budget lines, tax-exempt properties, billing and delinquency, and a public message for Town Meeting. The only votes were approving the January 23rd minutes and adjourning.

budget_items.what_was_said: The consultant's draft offers fee alternatives with differing values per equivalent residential unit, plus a tier structure.
A member's preliminary budget shows personnel alone consuming much of the needed revenue, and one-time equipment purchases were noted.
Members noted Chapter 90 is state money for specific projects, not salaries, and one member listed expected yearly amounts.

budget_items.topic: Existing town budget stormwater lines offset
budget_items.what_was_said: A member argued the existing town drainage and stormwater budget lines should be subtracted from what residents are shown as the new cost; others noted the money would be reallocated, not removed.
Using the commercial alternative and the single/multi-family alternative gives a total that, with Chapter 90, comes near the consultant's original ask.
Members leaned toward adding the charge to the property tax bill to keep overhead down, and cited a monthly household amount.
Sewer delinquency is handled with a demand fee and daily interest and a lien after a year; the delinquency rate was cited, and the sewer minimum bill was compared to the stormwater charge.
Members favored keeping residents near the lowest tier and weighting commercial tiers higher.
A member estimated the added yearly cost to a large commercial site.

decisions.decision: The chair will get clarification from the consultant on the tier structure by the next meeting and email it to members.

Questions recorded for the consultant: where properties like the apartment complex fit, what to do about tax-exempt properties and churches, and a rewrite of the unclear section three paragraph; Jen asked for a breakdown of properties in each category.
Members will decide the public message for the Town Meeting update at the March and April meetings, avoiding dollar figures for now.
The Town Meeting warrant article to allow a report will be taken at the spring town meeting as a formality, with a PR campaign to follow.

what_happened.line: The task force found the consultant's first-draft stormwater fee tiers unclear and will get clarification from the consultant before the next meeting.
Members could not tell where multifamily, apartment, condo and commercial properties fall in the tiers, and thought too few large properties were counted.
Working backwards from a revenue target, members found the fee alternatives plus Chapter 90 come near the consultant's original ask; no resolution was reached.
Members leaned toward putting the charge on the property tax bill and weighting commercial tiers higher, keeping residents near the lowest tier.
The only votes were approving the January 23rd minutes and adjourning; the Town Meeting warrant article to allow a report is planned as a formality.

why_it_matters: A stormwater utility fee would be a new charge, and which tier a home, condo, apartment complex or business lands in decides what it pays, so the unclear tiers are the open question for any resident or owner.
Whether existing town drainage budget lines are netted against the new fee, and whether the charge rides on the tax bill, changes what residents are shown as the new cost and how it is collected.
